chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: The musician as community member; brotherhood and factions
summary: They discuss musicians as community figures, splintering into style cults, and the brotherhood that survives in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: That's the way it should be.
A musician should be -- community members and work with the community.
That's the way it was in ancient times.
They weren't as set apart as -- we now sort of -- a lot of musicians think they're so different.

From back -- yeah, we're so different and we go back and we kind of ostracize ourselves, like we were -- you were saying before, different styles and then you get a different cult, where each style and things like that, so you get so many different factions until you don't -- we don't really recognize each other like we should.
I got in on the tail end of that.
Right, right. Oh, man, I mean, that was when -- and then, you find a lot of that in New Orleans now, but the older --

Right, right. And they're proud of each other, and they -- when they come away from there, I've had some musicians work with me and every year they have to make a trip back down there, and then they come back and tell you how well everybody's doing. It's just great.
